newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Degussa shares climb on profit gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Degussa shares climb on profit gain.

text.p: Chemicals and metals group Degussa AG, reaping benefits from a major restructuring and improved economic conditions, on Tuesday posted sharply higher quarterly profits, boosting its share price by two percent.
Management board chairman Uwe-Ernst Bufe told a news conference that group pre-tax profits jumped 20 percent during the first quarter of the 1996/1997 business year ending September 30.
This puts the group on track to outpace last year's earnings, Bufe said.
First quarter sales climbed 16 percent, Degussa said, declining to give more specific figures.

"We expect (to post) a higher profit rate than the two to three percent rise (posted) for the whole (1995/1996) year but this will probably be a little lower than the 20 percent rate" posted in the first quarter, chief financial officer Heinz-Joachim Wagner later told Reuters in an interview.
Investors, delighted with both the numbers and optimistic outlook, turned Degussa into one of the day's best share market performers, ending bourse trade 15 marks higher at 730 marks.
This outpaced the German market's 30-share blue chip index, which closed bourse trading down 1.78 percent.

Analysts credit Degussa's new board members, including Bufe and Wagner, with an overhaul of the corporate structure and with new, ambitious financial goals which are helping to erase the group's formerly stodgy reputation.
"In light (of the changes), Degussa appears to be be putting itself in a position to report overproportionally strong profit growth in coming years," said MM Warburg analyst Sven Dopke.
Several analysts predicted the group's share price could soar as high as 800 marks, continuing to outperform the sector.

Degussa expects all core business areas, chemical products, health and nutrition and precious metals and banking, will post strong gains in the future as the acquisition of U.S. drugs group Muro Pharmaceuticals and a completed restructuring in the precious metals area pay dividends.

After receiving U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval to launch an allergy medicine already sold in Germany and Asia in the U.S. market, Degussa expects significant progress in its health products area.
"The drug is used to treat hay fever and in a nation as large as the U.S. there are going to be a lot of people having hay fever all the time," said board member Heribert Offermanns.

The group also spent 60 million marks ($37 million) to completely overhaul the precious metals area, Bufe said, adding Degussa had earned nearly 50 million marks from sales of four tonnes of gold and 250 tonnes of silver last year.

In the 1995/1996 business year Degussa posted a one percent drop in sales to 13.8 billion marks and a two percent rise in pre-tax profits to 413 million marks as sluggish industry conditions took their toll.

Setting his sights on ongoing strong exports and business abroad, especially in North and South America, Bufe said Degussa was now benefiting from the much stronger dollar as many precious metals were quoted in dollars.
"The higher the dollar, the better for us," Bufe said.
At the same time Degussa also appears to have completed its divestment and acquisition plans for now.

"What we have today, we would like to continue to keep, running it on our own or with a partner," Bufe said. Board member Guenter Wohlenberg added Degussa would be ready to make smaller acquisitions but had no major plans at present.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($1=1.6223 Mark)
